summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 2.2/109)

data.turoyo: Ya u ṣəroyo əzzewo, mṭahriwo aṭ ṭaye u naʕimaṯṯe b sefe, huwewo Kəriv ʕam u ṭayo, haṯe yo.
data.translation: Or the Christian would go; the Muslims would circumcise their children in his lap, and he would become kəriv with the Muslim. That is it.

rationale: First Infectum-wa box; explicit children as patients disambiguate the customary lap-holding role.

summary: New box Part. Pass.: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (Jan 2.26/4448)

data.turoyo: Xori Brahim: Lə šaməʕno. Bas azzən ḥərre, kəlle mṭahro.
data.translation: Father Brahim: I have not heard. But they went and looked, there he was, circumcised.

rationale: First Detransitive Part. Pass. box and explicit circumcised-state sense.
mṭahro predicates the man’s visible circumcised state after they go and look; no causing agent is expressed. One clear Part. Pass. token supplies the Detransitive counterpart.

data.turoyo: Kəriv hani, d kəmṭahri aṭ ṭaye b sefe d ḥḏoḏe, kowən Kəriv.
data.translation: Those kəriv, the Muslims circumcise one another in their laps, and they become kəriv.

rationale: Thin Infectum cell; reciprocal lap possessors and circumcision sponsors, with the child patient implicit. Machine English one another is not taken as a literal adult patient.

summary: All three occurrences receive decisions. No round-1 run exists; the inherited active Infectum example is the baseline.

Active circumcision has children as overt or understood patients. b sefe is the lap location/holder’s role, already represented in the inherited example, not an instrument or a separate circumcise-on-lap sense.

The Muslims as grammatical active subjects need not identify the individual who performs the surgery; circumcision sponsorship can be reported by the same verb. The source does not distinguish surgeon from parent/ritual sponsor.
Infectum-wa gives customary repeated practice. mṭahro profiles a visible state without an expressed causing agent and supports a separate Detransitive section.

The first machine English says circumcise one another. Turoyo b sefe d ḥḏoḏe makes reciprocity modify laps, and the later explicit u naʕimaṯṯe clarifies children as patients; the English is preserved rather than rewritten.
No new idiom, active sense, etymology change or speculative religious-affiliation sense is added. English is supplied machine translation.
In kəmṭahri aṭ ṭaye b sefe d ḥḏoḏe, confirm the omitted child patients and the sponsor versus actual operator roles; the machine English one another obscures the lap construction.
Confirm mṭahro as masculine Part. Pass. and whether its visible-state interpretation is the ordinary Detransitive paradigm; only one such token is supplied.
